annotation.title_clean: 14 CFR Part 21—Certification Procedures for Products and Articles
annotation.title_en: 14 CFR Part 21—Certification Procedures for Products and Articles
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), U.S. Department of Transportation
annotation.summary_en: US Federal Aviation Regulations Part 21 sets certification procedures for aircraft, engines, propellers and articles: type, supplemental type and production certificates, airworthiness approvals, TSO authorizations, failure reporting and quality systems. It contains no AI or robotics-specific provisions, and is only tangentially relevant to certification of physical systems.
key_provisions_or_claims: Type certificates require showing compliance with airworthiness, noise, emissions and fuel efficiency requirements.
Production certificate holders must maintain an FAA-approved quality system.
Certificate holders must report failures, malfunctions and defects to the FAA within 24 hours.
Special conditions apply for novel or unusual design features.
TSO authorizations and PMA govern approval of articles and parts.
